lines.text: I rent a flat in Bengaluru, which means I have a landlord, and he has a plan.
Last November he promised he would fix the water heater by winter.
He didn't say which winter.
This winter, I'm hoping for global warming.
My family has a group chat with forty-three people in it.
In six years, nobody has asked a single question.
It's just good morning flowers, from uncles who have never bought a flower.
At five in the morning. Uncle, the flowers aren't even awake.
My dad only has three moods.
Hungry, cricket, and disappointed in me.
On a good day, he manages all three at dinner.
So yeah, I've been trying to get fit lately, I guess.
There's a gym near my place, it's pretty big, they have machines.
Some days I go, some days I don't, you know how it is.
Anyway, the gym is fine, it's a gym.
Um, what else, okay, traffic here is bad, right.
It takes forever to get anywhere, basically.
So that's traffic.
I'm back on the dating apps, which are job portals with better lighting.
Every single profile says they love travelling.
Sir, you went to Goa once, in 2016, with your office.
I mean, travelling is nice, I like trains too.
My mother got a smart speaker, and she treats it like a new daughter-in-law.
She tells it to play the news.
She tells it to switch off the fan.
She tells it nobody in this house listens to her. It says, okay.
She's never been happier. She's thinking of moving in with it.
My cousin quit his job to build an app that reminds you to drink water.
He has raised four crore.
My grandmother has done that job for free since 1962.
An Indian wedding has three days of events.
The haldi, the sangeet, and the wedding.
And one uncle at all three, asking when I'm getting married.
My sister just started a new job at a bank.
First day, she calls me, very excited, she's met her new boss.
It's my landlord. He promised her a promotion by winter.
Last Sunday, India lost a final, right at dinner time.
All three of my dad's moods, on one plate.
Anyway, my landlord says I can stay another year.
He didn't say which year.
You've been lovely. Goodnight!
